(1) Poly-encoders achieve state-of-the art performance, (2) Bi-encoders are more accurate than Cross-encodes on some datasets, (3) Cross-encoders are slower than Bi-encodes, and (4) Poly-encodes are faster than Crossencodes.

(1) Poly-encoders, a new transformer architecture that learns global rather then token level self-attendance features, (2) are faster and more accurate than Cross-encodes, (3) and Bi-encodes; (4) and the best results are achieved by pre-training on datasets similar to the down stream task.
Poly-encodes are faster than Cross and more accurate than bi encoders and pre-training on a large dataset similar to the downstream task is the best strategy for all three approaches.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following three questions: What pre-training and fine tuning strategies work best for multi-sentence scoring tasks? How can we build fast and accurate models for such tasks? What is the role of self-attention in multi-sentence scoring?
the following questions: How can we design efficient transformer models that are competitive with Cross-encoders? How can we best pre-train and fine-tune such models?
the design of a new transformer architecture and pre-training strategies that lead to fast and accurate models for a variety of tasks.

(1) Poly-encoders can be used for a wide variety of tasks, and (2) Poly-encodings are faster than Cross encoders and more accurate that Bi-encoders.
Poly-encodes are faster, more accurate and more efficient than both Cross-encoders, Bi-encoders and other state-of-the-art approaches.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a new transformer architecture for multi-sentence matching, Poly-encoder, which is faster than Cross-encoder and more accurate than the Bi-encoder.

Poly-encodings are faster and more accurate than bi-encodings and cross-encodings, and that pre-training on a dataset that is similar to the downstream task is more beneficial than pre-training on a large general-purpose dataset.
Poly-encoder is a fast and accurate model that is easy to use and pre-train.
The main takeaway from our work is that

Bi-encoders, when properly pre-trained and fine-tuned, are a viable alternative to Cross-encoders, and that Poly-encodings are a new, fast and powerful architecture that can be used for many applications.
, for tasks where the input is a pair of sequences, the best approach is to pre-train a Cross-encoder on a large corpus of pairs and then use a Poly-encoder to score pairs at test time.
